1) Suicide in children and adolescents is very frequently the outcome of a serious mental disorder, particularly when associated to drug and alcohol abuse, and 2) the presence of two or multiple mental disorders (comorbidities) was the rule in children and adolescents who completed suicide.
Comorbid psychiatric disorders are common in children and adolescents who commit suicide.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a model to explain how a combination of genetic, environmental, and psychological factors can contribute to the development of a mental disorder and to suicide in children and youth.
the development of an integrated model of the etiology, prevention, and intervention of suicide in adolescents.
the development and evaluation of a comprehensive model of the etiology and treatment of adolescent suicide, and its implementation in a community-based program.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
suicide is the outcome of a complex interaction of multiple variables, including the biological, psychological and social.
the presence of a single mental disorder in a child is not predictive of suicide.

suicide in children is the result of a serious mental disorder, which may be a mood disorder or a conduct disorder, which may or may not coexist with alcohol and drug abuse and/or other mental disorders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
suicide in children is not a single disease but is a complex of diseases that may be related to the presence of a mood disorder and comorbidity with other mental disorders.
suicide is a serious and preventable problem in the adolescent age group.
suicide in children, adolescents, and young adults is the outcome of severe psychiatric disorders, particularly mood disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should not be afraid of the diagnosis of mental health problems in our patients.

the most common mental disorders in children and adolescents who committed suicide were mood disorders, such as major depressive disorder, major depressive disorder superimposed on persistent depressive disorder and persistent depressive disorder.
suicide is not a random event, but is associated with a variety of mental health conditions.
